summary: Re-review after repairs. The round-1 critical (medication-adherence q008 once-daily contradiction) and both majors (anchoring versus premature closure in attention-and-perception q007, anchoring versus confirmation bias in memory-and-decision-making q002) are fixed, and most round-1 minors were also repaired (sick role now has four elements, OCD is separated from the anxiety disorders, AUDIT items 9-10 are scored correctly, capacity and consent lessons now cover presumption, two-stage test, advance decisions and Gillick). No literal '[object Object]', empty list items or null placeholders were found in any packet. Facts, keys and recomputed numerics all check out and no unsafe clinical advice was found. Remaining problems are minor: padding-style trivial or near-duplicate arithmetic/count questions, pseudo-formulas and undefined symbols in math blocks, math-block delimiter and prose-in-latex hygiene, and an unnamed classification system for GAD duration. This is an AI review only; the course still needs a subject-matter expert before clinical reliance.

issues.problem: The math block shows 'Delta V = alpha beta (lambda - V)' (Rescorla-Wagner) but alpha, beta, lambda and V are never defined and the equation is not used in the lesson or questions; it is beyond the unit's objectives for a Year 2 student.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the equation, or define each symbol and add a one-line explanation of what it predicts.

issues.problem: The math block 'MI = partnership + acceptance + compassion + evocation' and 'HBM: (susceptibility + severity + ...) > barriers' presents invented arithmetic as if MI and the HBM were additive formulas. Neither is quantitative in this way.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace with a plain list or callout (the four MI spirit elements and the HBM constructs) or label clearly as a mnemonic, not a formula.

issues.problem: GAD is stated to need '>= 6 months' and specific phobia 'often >= 6 months' without naming the system. That is the DSM-5 criterion; ICD-10 requires symptoms on most days for at least several weeks, usually months. The preceding depression unit explicitly labels ICD-10 versus DSM-5, so this unit is inconsistent. The math block '6 months = 26 weeks' is also arithmetic padding.
issues.suggestedFix: State 'DSM-5: 6 months; ICD-10: several weeks, usually months', and drop the pseudo-math block.

issues.problem: q003 (34 weeks minus 26) and q008 (20 weeks, 6 more needed) are near-duplicate week-subtraction questions that test arithmetic, not the objective of differentiating GAD, panic disorder and specific phobia.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace one or both with a distinguishing-features or treatment question.

issues.problem: q003 and q009 are near-duplicate reverse-scoring arithmetic questions on an invented subscale; neither addresses the unit objectives (ICE, common-sense model, culture).
issues.suggestedFix: Keep one and replace the other with an ICE or cultural-context question.

issues.problem: q006 ('how many stages in the two-stage test') and q007 (count of abilities present) are recall-by-count items with trivial value; the same pattern recurs in consent q004/q008, illness-behaviour q005/q007 (stage count) and depression q004/q009.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace counting questions with application items (for example, a vignette asking which functional ability fails).

issues.problem: The adjustment sequence is taught as six stages by splitting 'shock/disbelief' from 'denial'. The Kubler-Ross model usually has five stages (denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance), so a count question keyed 6 depends on a lesson-specific variant.
issues.suggestedFix: Drop the count question, or present the five-stage model and treat shock as an early reaction rather than a separate stage.

issues.problem: q009 invents a 'harm-reduction programme' that cuts stimulant craving episodes from 12 to 3 per week; harm reduction does not by itself aim at or reliably produce this. q003 and q006 are likewise invented numbers, and q003/q009 say 'Give your answer as a number and % sign' on a numeric item.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace with a question on mechanisms of opioid substitution or naloxone, and ask for numeric answers in % without the sign instruction.

issues.problem: q006 (28% of 500 receptors remain free) is a trivial percentage calculation built on a made-up 'receptor count'; it adds nothing to the dopamine-hypothesis objective and could teach a misleading idea that receptors are counted clinically.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace with a question on mesolimbic versus nigrostriatal D2 blockade and the link to positive symptoms and EPS.

issues.problem: Several math blocks still wrap latex in '\[ ... \]' delimiters (medication-adherence, consent-and-mental-health-law, depression-and-bipolar, alcohol-use) and some embed prose ('where s_i in ...', multi-line symptom thresholds) in the latex field; these may render poorly in KaTeX (unverified). The stress-response block also contains a blank line inside the latex string.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the delimiter wrappers, move explanatory prose into the caption or a text block, and remove the blank line; check rendering.
